title: Highly efficient, durable and eco-friendly intumescent flame retardant for wool fabrics
washing_state: Untreated source control after initial cleaning; no durability washing
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Cut and crushed wool fabric aliquot; section 8 untreated and treated wool with 27.4% WG
source_material_form_LOI_raw: Wool fabric; Table 2 initial 0 LCs state; oven dried before LOI
treatment_method: 100% woven wool fabric, 130 g/m², acquired in Jilin city, China. Before modification the source fabric was rinsed to remove surface impurities and oven dried; rinse details and initial drying temperature/duration are not stated. No ANPP treatment is assigned to the control.
TGA_specimen_preparation: Fabric was cut and crushed before placement in a small crucible. The methods specify approximately 5–6 mg of the treated sample; a separate control mass is not stated. Crucible material and instrument model are not reported.
LOI_uncertainty: ±0.3; source does not define SD, SE or another statistic
LOI_locator: Published p.1003, PDF p.5, Table 2, 0 LCs row; p.1004 section 5 repeats the four initial LOIs; abstract and p.1012 conclusion repeat the 27.4% WG state.
TG_locator: Published p.1010, PDF p.12, Table 6; p.1009 section 8 explicitly assigns TG to untreated wool and treated wool with 27.4% WG; Figure 10 shows both atmospheres.
conditions_locator: Published pp.1000–1001: Experimental sections 1–4; p.1002 Table 1 and section 2 map 30% ANPP solution to 27.4% WG; p.1010 defines T10 and Tmax.
pairing_evidence: Table 6 untreated row and Table 2 untreated 0 LCs row identify the same cleaned source fabric.
source_access_method: Official Korean Institute of Chemical Engineers fifteen-page PDF downloaded from its public article download link. Full original text reviewed; preparation, LOI Table 2, TG Table 6, Figure 10 and assay-method page pixels checked.
limitations: Only untreated wool and the 27.4% WG initial treated fabric have own TG. Table 1 and section 2 map this treated state to a nominal 30% ANPP solution, but the basis of that solution percentage is not stated; do not convert it to g/L or final material fraction. Table 2 uses 0 LCs for initial LOI; the preparation includes a flowing-water rinse, which is retained as a process wash. The later durability LOIs are not paired to baseline TG. LOI ± values and Table 1 WG ± values have no stated statistical definition or replicate count; no SD or n is invented. Five repetitions in the whiteness/tensile methods are not assigned to LOI or TG. The TG mass sentence explicitly says treated sample, so the control mass remains unspecified. LOI drying at 80 °C for 4 h is not silently assigned to TG. The source contains unrelated interpretation errors, including type I cellulose and L-glucose language for wool, a later 33.7% WG typo versus the defined 35.7% state, and a two-stage description of treated air degradation despite two tabulated rate peaks plus initial moisture loss; these are preserved as source limitations and not used to repair the numerical tables. The extracted PDF text layer contains an INVITED REVIEW PAPER white-text header artifact, invisible on the rendered first page. The body supplies its own Experimental section, original measured tables, and an ANPP row explicitly marked This work in Table 5; publication type is journal_article and only those own measurements are used. The synthesis prose mentions 200 mL of 5% KMnO4 solution for formaldehyde absorption without a clear apparatus arrangement; no alternate synthesis arrangement is inferred.
